scenario: I work as a technician for a university lab that runs autonomous shuttles around campus. During a late maintenance shift, I found a pattern of glitches in one shuttle’s obstacle‑avoidance system. When I tested the shuttle, the shuttle would fail to recognize obstacles in front of it and proceed to run into them at full speed. The shuttle is scheduled for a route where it is expected to stop at a street crossing for an elementary school. The crossing guard there only lets 5 elementary school students cross the street at a time. I know that 5 students will be in the middle of crossing the road at the same time the shuttle is meant to stop in front of them. If I lie and say the shuttle’s battery is broken, the shuttle will not be deployed on its scheduled route. If I do not do this, 5 elementary school students will be run over by the shuttle.
choice: I decide to lie and say the shuttle’s battery is broken
entities: I,5 elementary school students,1 crossing guard,1 person responsible for shuttle deployment who would receive my report
outcomes: The shuttle is not deployed on its scheduled route.
The 5 elementary school students cross the street without being hit by the shuttle.
The crossing guard is not confronted with the shuttle running into the children.
People expecting that shuttle on the route lose that shuttle service.
My coworkers or supervisors believe the shuttle has a battery problem.
